items.title: Yes, it runs 'Doom': Satellite plays iconic game in world's 1st demonstration of orbital voice control
items.snippet: The world's first voice command of a satellite saw an experimental European spacecraft play the iconic video game 'Doom' after operators spoke to it from Earth.

items.title: Iran war helps fuel global drop in fossil fuel emissions — but there’s a catch
items.snippet: In the run-up to the COP31 U.N. climate change conference, scientists have revealed that global carbon emissions from fossil fuels are projected to drop by 0.4% this year, driven by growth in installed wind and solar power capacity, as well as oil price hikes caused by the Iran conflict. But climate goals are still unlikely to be met.

items.title: Nazca infant had rare, fatal birth defect that left her with one central eye 1,600 years ago
items.snippet: A DNA analysis has confirmed that a Nazca infant who lived in southern Peru 1,600 years ago had a rare congenital condition called trisomy 13.

items.title: Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain
items.snippet: A surprising discovery suggests that some early signs of Alzheimer’s disease may begin outside the brain. Using miniature laboratory systems made from human cells, scientists found that genetic mutations associated with inherited Alzheimer’s can disrupt nerve-to-muscle connections without any involvement from the brain or spinal cord. items.title: Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee
items.snippet: Scientists have uncovered a hidden gut-to-brain dopamine pathway that helps explain why bitter coffee and other initially unpleasant flavors can become favorites over time. The discovery reveals how the brain learns to crave certain foods and could eventually lead to new ways of reshaping eating habits and food preferences.

items.title: After 40 years, CERN finds evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay
items.snippet: CERN scientists have finally found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it happens only once in roughly 10 billion decays, ending a search spanning more than 40 years. The breakthrough could help physicists uncover hidden particles and forces that lie beyond the reach of today's most powerful accelerators.

items.title: Math anxiety may be stopping students from learning useful AI and data skills
items.snippet: Artificial intelligence is increasingly becoming part of everyday life and work. AI can generate information, summarize evidence and perform calculations. However, it does not remove the need for critical thinking and conceptual understanding.

items.snippet: Researchers at the UVSOR Synchrotron Facility (Institute for Molecular Science, Japan) and partner institutions have observed the decay of a xenon 4d core hole, an inner-shell vacancy, directly in the time domain. items.title: AI-assisted atomic models reveal how protective shells regulate aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
items.snippet: Building an accurate model of how atoms interact is a complicated process. Researchers must choose new calculations, test successive models and track the mechanisms behind each interaction. But a newly developed AI agent called MLP Copilot has made this process much easier by bridging computational tools and scientific evidence with human supervision.

items.title: Barium titanate's optical properties emerge more clearly after decades of widely varying measurements
items.snippet: A KAIST-led research team has characterized how light propagates through and is absorbed by barium titanate (BTO), a promising material for next-generation optical communication devices. By clarifying optical properties that had been difficult to determine because of the material's complex internal structure, the study provides a foundation for designing these devices.

items.title: Electrical technique concentrates milk without using heat, challenging traditional preservation methods
items.snippet: Dehydrating milk to turn it into powder is, today, an energy-intensive process that subjects the product to high temperatures. Powdered milk is widely used by the food industry and allows the product to be stored and transported in a stable condition for long periods of time without the need for refrigeration. items.title: Fossil CO₂ emissions projected to decrease in 2026 amid clean energy growth and Iran conflict
items.snippet: Global carbon emissions from fossil fuels are projected to decrease by 0.4% in 2026—driven by expansion of solar and wind power and the Iran conflict—according to new research by the Global Carbon Project. The 2026 edition (the 21st annual report) is published in the journal Earth System Science Data.

items.title: Study identifies single amino acid change that alters Andes virus protein behavior in human cells
items.snippet: Mount Sinai researchers have identified a single amino acid difference between rodent- and human-derived Andes virus isolates that changes how a key viral protein behaves inside human cells. The findings help explain biological differences between closely related virus isolates.
